title: Lanterns: Episode 6 unveils corporate Green Lantern
seoTitle: Lanterns: Episode 6 unveils corporate Green Lantern
subtitle: The sixth episode of "Lanterns" shakes the DC universe with the introduction of a sponsored hero and the investigation into Hal Jordan's death.
excerpt: The release of the "Bad Optics" episode of "Lanterns" brought major twists, including Guy Gardner's rise as a corporate‑backed Green Lantern.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The DC universe is buzzing with the launch of the sixth episode of "Lanterns," titled "Bad Optics," which delivered crucial twists and deepened the complex dynamics of its heroes, generating huge interest and online searches. The series, inspired by productions like "True Detective," "Training Day," and "Banshee," intensifies its plot with the return of John Stewart and the brand‑new figure of Guy Gardner.

The return of John Stewart and the investigation

In 2026, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), who had abandoned his Green Lantern ring in the previous episode, returns to Rushville to investigate the death of Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler). His quest for answers and personal closure leads him into a tangled web of events, where Hal's consciousness—previously a projection—is reactivated to assist the investigation. This twist ensures Kyle Chandler's continued presence in the series even after his character's death.

To solve the mystery, John needs Hal's deactivated ring, which is held by the Guardians of the Universe. He turns to Guy Gardner to retrieve the artifact, using guilt as a tactic by reminding him that Guy's position as Earth’s Green Lantern exists only because John turned it down a decade earlier. Reluctant, Guy yields to the pressure, establishing a tense dynamic between the two.

Guy Gardner: the corporate lantern

Nathan Fillion plays Guy Gardner, a Green Lantern who stands out for his "classic‑comic" approach and his corporate side. After John Stewart declined the chance to become Earth’s Green Lantern, the Guardians chose Gardner as his successor. It is suggested that they, possibly together with Gardner’s corporate benefactor Maxwell Lord, sought to rehabilitate the Green Lantern image after the traumatic events in Rushville.

Gardner is portrayed as both a superhero and a corporate mascot, endorsing an energy drink. Fillion explains that Guy sees marketing as part of his role, aligning his personal goal of opening a bar with the need for corporate sponsorship. He installed a version of the Bat‑Signal in Rushville—a Green Lantern beacon—to try to remedy the previous destruction, an initiative that, according to Fillion, received support from LordTech’s public‑relations teams.

James Gunn's vision for the DCU

Director and co‑CEO of DC Studios James Gunn argues that the DC Universe (DCU) will not have a single style, allowing each character and story to reflect distinct tones, just like the comics. Nathan Fillion, who has worked on twelve projects with Gunn, had no concerns about inserting Guy Gardner, with his quirky haircut, into a series with a more serious tone. He compared the experience to visiting Metropolis and Gotham: the same person, but with very different weekends.

Fillion praises Gunn's ability to tell stories on multiple levels, highlighting his growth as a professional without losing his essence. Gunn's skill at navigating different tones is crucial for integrating characters like Guy Gardner, who have a more caricatured aesthetic, into the gritty world of "Lanterns".

The future of Guy Gardner and the DC universe

Nathan Fillion not only stars in "Lanterns" but will also reprise his role as Guy Gardner in James Gunn's 2027 "Superman" sequel, titled "Man of Tomorrow." Additionally, he will voice Gardner in the animated series "Mister Miracle."

Regarding "Man of Tomorrow," Fillion anticipates that the film, after focusing on Superman in the first feature, will delve deeper into Lex Luthor, whom he considers equally important to the narrative. This expansion of characters and the interconnection between productions reinforce the DCU's strategy of building a cohesive, multifaceted universe.

With information from The Hollywood Reporter, IndieWire, Variety.
